Is there anything I can do to help get this merged in?
I'm not a code owner either, don't own any flo device, and I havent seen any other logs..

The original logged traceback can be found here (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/89830#issue-1628258492) in the ticket that spawned this ticket.

It does appear that the upstream client library aioflo calls aiohttp.ClientResponse.json() and does not catch the JSONDecodeError. So I think as @ViViDboarder suggests this is the best that can be done right now.

The code in question can be found here https://github.com/bachya/aioflo/blob/dev/aioflo/api.py -
```
        try:
            async with session.request(method, url, **kwargs) as resp:
                data: dict = await resp.json(content_type=None)
                resp.raise_for_status()
                return data
        except ClientError as err:
            raise RequestError(f"There was an error while requesting {url}") from err
        finally:
            if not use_running_session:
                await session.close()
```

@kchiem I am seeing this error intermittently as well. I am also running 2023.3.4 and HA OS. I have 1 flo valve and 7 remote water sensor pucks. Most of the time it works fine. It just occasionally has a trace back like yours above.

If this turns out to be an issue with the upstream API and these failures just happen occasionally I'd love to see the traceback caught to reduce the log noise. Something like the following -
```
diff --git a/homeassistant/components/flo/device.py b/homeassistant/components/flo/device.py
index 1b28a2552a..7c452fb382 100644
--- a/homeassistant/components/flo/device.py
+++ b/homeassistant/components/flo/device.py
@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@
 from __future__ import annotations
 
 from datetime import datetime, timedelta
+from json import JSONDecodeError
 from typing import Any
 
 from aioflo.api import API
@@ -45,6 +46,8 @@ class FloDeviceDataUpdateCoordinator(DataUpdateCoordinator):
                 await self._update_consumption_data()
         except RequestError as error:
             raise UpdateFailed(error) from error
+        except JSONDecodeError as error:
+            raise UpdateFailed(error) from error
 
     @property
     def location_id(self) -> str:
```

This transforms the traceback into the following -
```
ERROR (MainThread) [custom_components.flo] Error fetching flo-XXXXXXXXXXXX data: unexpected character: line 1 column 1 (char 0)
```
